summary: Clackamas County, OR: 1929 20-ft tower, 1933 L-4 cab, removed by 1967; 2016 article says the summit road now serves radio antennas where the lookout stood, and the summit trail is closed.

corrections.why: Firetower.org, firelookout.com and the WyEast Blog all describe the 1929 tower as 20 feet (about 6.1 m). No source reviewed gives 50 feet (15.2 m). The height of the 1933 L-4 cab is not stated, so this is low confidence.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rex's page says the lookout was deactivated in 1964; firetower.org, firelookout.com and the WyEast Blog say it was gone or removed by 1967. Both dates are kept as separate events, since deactivation and removal are different steps.

sources.title: A New Vision: Restoring Hiyu Mountain

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 15.2 (50 ft) conflicts with the 20-ft 1929 tower in all sources; see corrections (low confidence, because the L-4 cab height is not given). Brief elevation 1,418 m matches firetower.org. Access is 'closed' because the WyEast Blog says the Forest Service closed the summit trail; the 2016 article is the latest source, so this may be out of date. The story does not recommend the trail. The 1934 fall is recorded without the employee's name. One web search turned up Dog Mountain (WA) and Lookout Mountain (Hood River) pages, which are different sites and were not used. Photos are not recorded as new finds because no image URLs were collected.
